lessons.unit: Spring 1: Common vocabulary: numbers, colours, clothes and shapes
lessons.title: Bridge: long vowels and greetings
lessons.bigQuestion: How do Muslims greet each other, and why does it matter?
objectives: To understand how long vowels are written and how to greet and reply politely in Arabic
successCriteria: All: read the long vowels ا و ي in words
Most: greet and reply for morning, evening and goodbye
Some: reply to a greeting with a better one
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: good manners and first impressions
lessons.smsc: Social: spreading salam builds love and community

keywords.def: long vowel letters: ا و ي

hook.text: Muslims all over the world greet with the same words. Why do you think one greeting matters so much?
hook.a: It is a du'a for peace; it unites Muslims; Allah tells us to return greetings well.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with one better than it, or return it' (an-Nisa' 4:86).

starter.q: Bismillah. How do we read كُتُب? A) kataba B) kutub

teach.heading: Long vowels
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Hold the long vowel for two counts. The letter after the vowel (ا و ي) makes it long.

teach.heading: Hear the difference

misconception.wrong: قَلَم and قَالَ sound the same
misconception.right: قَلَم (qalam) has a short a; قَالَ (qala) has a long a written with ا

teach.note: Pupils hold up 1 finger for short, 2 for long as you read pairs.

teach.heading: Greetings and replies
teach.note: Spot the long vowels in each: سَلَام, صَبَاح, نُور.

teach.heading: A better reply
teach.note: Pupils practise the full reply.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: The reply to صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ is:
check.why: Morning greeting, morning reply: صَبَاحُ النُّورِ (morning of light).

practice.q: Read and find the long vowel: نُور
practice.a: nur; the long vowel is و (uu)
practice.model:
نُ = nu.
The و after a dammah makes it long: nuu.
ر = r.
Together: nur.

independent.q: Core: Write a six-line dialogue: salam and reply, how are you and reply, goodbye and reply.
independent.a: اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ بِخَيْرٍ، وَالحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first two lines, reading them with a pupil.

independent.q: Extend: Dictation: سَلَام، نُور، دِين، بَاب. Circle the long vowels.
independent.a: سَلَام (ا)، نُور (و)، دِين (ي)، بَاب (ا)

independent.q: Stretch: Perform your dialogue with a partner in a breakout room, using the better reply.
independent.a: Fluent dialogue with وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ

exit.q: Which letter makes a long 'ii'? A) ا B) و C) ي
Big question: how do Muslims greet each other, and why does it matter?
exit.a: With as-salamu 'alaykum; Allah tells us to return greetings with better (an-Nisa' 4:86), and it spreads peace.

lessons.homework: Greet your family in Arabic every morning and evening this week; write the greetings in your book.
lessons.send: SEND: greeting cards with replies on the back. EAL: transliteration and English on the cards. Stretch: explain why صَبَاحُ النُّورِ is a 'better' reply.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Common vocabulary: numbers, colours, clothes and shapes
lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 20 and my age
lessons.bigQuestion: How does Arabic build the numbers from 11 to 20?
objectives: To understand how to say, read and write the numbers 1 to 20 and use them to give my age
successCriteria: All: count from 1 to 10 and read the digits ١ to ١٠
Most: say 11 to 20 using the pattern 'one-ten'
Some: give my age correctly: عُمْرِي اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: place value; the digits used in Britain spread to Europe from the Arabic-speaking world
lessons.smsc: Cultural: Muslim mathematicians such as al-Khwarizmi and the spread of the number system

hook.text: In Arabic, 15 is 'five-ten' (خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ). Which English numbers follow a similar pattern?
hook.a: The '-teen' numbers: fifteen is five + ten.

islamicLink.text: Allah made the sun and moon so that we know the number of years and how to count time (Yunus 10:5). Counting in Arabic is a skill Muslims have used for prayer times, zakah and calendars.

starter.q: Bismillah. Which is Friday? A) الجُمُعَة B) الخَمِيس

teach.heading: 1 to 10 (recap)
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Add ٩ تِسْعَة and ١٠ عَشَرَة aloud. Pupils show fingers.

teach.heading: 11 to 15
teach.note: Pattern: unit + عَشَرَ. 11 and 12 are special: أَحَدَ and اِثْنَا.

teach.heading: 16 to 20
teach.note: 20 is a new word: عِشْرُونَ.

teach.heading: My age
bullets: كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ (kam 'umruka?) how old are you?
عُمْرِي اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً: I am twelve
عُمْرِي ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً: I am thirteen
teach.note: سَنَة (year) is feminine, so the numbers change form. Learn your own age as a fixed phrase.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model:
١٤ is four and ten.
Four: أَرْبَعَة, with -ata: أَرْبَعَةَ.
Add عَشَرَ: arba'ata 'ashar.

practice.q: Write twenty in Arabic digits and words.

independent.q: Core: Dictation of numbers: write the digits and words for 11, 13, 15, 18 and 20.
independent.a: ١١ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ؛ ١٣ ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ؛ ١٥ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ؛ ١٨ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ؛ ٢٠ عِشْرُونَ
independent.model: Teacher says أَحَدَ عَشَرَ, writes ١١, then the words, sounding each letter.

independent.q: Extend: Solve and write in Arabic words: ١٠ + ٦ = ? and ٢٠ − ٨ = ?
Stretch: Write a short profile: name, age, where you live: اِسْمِي ... عُمْرِي ... أَسْكُنُ فِي ...
independent.a: For example: اِسْمِي سَارَةُ. عُمْرِي اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً. أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ.

exit.q: What is عِشْرُونَ? A) 12 B) 20 C) 10
Big question: how does Arabic build 11 to 19?
exit.a: The unit number plus عَشَرَ (ten), e.g. خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ = 15; 11 and 12 have special forms.

lessons.homework: Read the page numbers of a book aloud in Arabic up to 20, and write your age and two family members' ages in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: number line ١ to ٢٠ with words. EAL: number cards with English. Stretch: count in twos to 20 in Arabic.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Common vocabulary: personal pronouns, my family, adjectives and moods
lessons.title: My family: relatives in Arabic
lessons.bigQuestion: What is the most important thing a family gives each other?
objectives: To understand and use the core family words to introduce my family
successCriteria: All: name six family members
Most: say هٰذَا أَبِي / هٰذِهِ أُمِّي
Some: describe a family of five in three sentences
lessons.smsc: Moral: respect for family

hook.text: What is the most important thing a family gives each other?
hook.a: Love, care and respect: Islam honours parents greatly.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents' (al-'Ankabut 29:8).

teach.heading: Family words
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. No pictures of people: use a family tree with boxes and words.

teach.heading: This is my ...
bullets: هٰذَا أَبِي: this is my father
هٰذِهِ أُمِّي: this is my mother
teach.note: Note: أَب → أَبِي, أَخ → أَخِي.

teach.heading: Family tree
teach.note: Boxes and words only.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model: Teacher: brother is a boy word: هٰذَا. أَخ + ـِي = أَخِي. Together: هٰذَا أَخِي.

independent.q: Family tree on the pupil PDF (boxes and words, no drawings of people): label your family (or an example family), then write four 'this is my ...' sentences.
independent.a: For example: هٰذَا أَبِي. هٰذِهِ أُمِّي. هٰذَا أَخِي. هٰذِهِ جَدَّتِي.
independent.model: Teacher fills the first two boxes and writes هٰذَا أَبِي.

independent.q: Extend: say how many brothers and sisters: عِنْدِي أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.
independent.a: Pupils' own with numbers

independent.q: Stretch: write 'my family is big' / 'small'.
independent.a: عَائِلَتِي كَبِيرَةٌ / صَغِيرَةٌ

exit.q: عَائِلَة is ...
Back to our ponder: what does a family give?

lessons.homework: Teach a family member five family words in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: family tree boxes with words to drag. EAL: word grid. Stretch: add عَمّ and خَال (next lesson).

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Common vocabulary: personal pronouns, my family, adjectives and moods
lessons.title: Describing people: looks and character
lessons.bigQuestion: Is it more important to describe what someone looks like or what they are like inside? Why?
objectives: To understand how to describe people's looks and character with adjectives that agree
successCriteria: All: use four adjectives of looks and character
Most: make adjectives agree with boys and girls
Some: describe a family member with three linked adjectives
lessons.smsc: Moral: valuing good character

hook.text: Is it more important to describe what someone looks like or what they are like inside? Why?
hook.a: Inside: Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not appearances (Muslim).

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah does not look at your appearance or wealth, but He looks at your hearts and deeds' (Muslim).

teach.heading: Looks and character
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Say: my brother is clever and generous.
practice.model: Teacher: أَخِي (boy) → ذَكِيٌّ and كَرِيمٌ, joined with وَ.

independent.q: Describe three family members on the pupil PDF (or in the portal response box): one look and one character adjective each, joined with وَ.
independent.a: For example: أَبِي طَوِيلٌ وَكَرِيمٌ. أُمِّي لَطِيفَةٌ وَذَكِيَّةٌ. أَخِي صَغِيرٌ وَمَرِحٌ.
independent.model: Teacher writes: أَبِي طَوِيلٌ وَكَرِيمٌ.

independent.q: Extend: add جِدًّا (very): أُمِّي لَطِيفَةٌ جِدًّا.
independent.a: Sentence with جِدًّا

independent.q: Stretch: why does Islam value character more than looks?
independent.a: Allah looks at our hearts and deeds (Muslim).

exit.q: كَرِيم means ...
Back to our ponder: looks or inside?
exit.a: Inside: Allah looks at hearts and deeds.

lessons.homework: Write four sentences describing your family's character.
lessons.send: SEND: adjective cards in two colours (boy / girl). EAL: adjective grid. Stretch: use جِدًّا and وَلٰكِنْ.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Common vocabulary: personal pronouns, my family, adjectives and moods
lessons.title: I have: عِنْدِي
lessons.bigQuestion: Arabic says 'with me is a brother' instead of 'I have a brother'. What does that show about how languages think?
objectives: To understand how to say what I have and what others have using عِنْدَ with endings
successCriteria: All: say عِنْدِي with a family word
Most: change عِنْدِي to عِنْدَكَ، عِنْدَهُ، عِنْدَهَا
Some: answer هَلْ عِنْدَكَ ...؟ with نَعَمْ / لَا

hook.text: Arabic says 'with me is a brother' instead of 'I have a brother'. What does that show about how languages think?
hook.a: Languages can say the same idea in different ways: عِنْدِي أَخٌ.

teach.heading: I have, you have ...
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Questions
bullets: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ أَخٌ؟ Do you have a brother?

teach.heading: With numbers
teach.note: Two: the dual ending ـَانِ.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model: Teacher: yes = نَعَمْ; I have = عِنْدِي; two sisters = أُخْتَانِ. Together: نَعَمْ، عِنْدِي أُخْتَانِ.

practice.q: Say 'I do not have a brother'.

independent.q: Survey grid on the pupil PDF: ask a partner (breakout) four هَلْ عِنْدَكَ ...؟ questions (brother, sister, cat, bicycle), record answers, then write four sentences about them with عِنْدَهُ / عِنْدَهَا.
independent.a: Questions asked; e.g. عِنْدَهُ أَخَوَانِ؛ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهَا قِطَّةٌ
independent.model: Teacher asks a pupil: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ دَرَّاجَةٌ؟ and writes the answer as عِنْدَهُ دَرَّاجَةٌ.

independent.q: Extend: write three sentences about what your family has.
independent.a: For example: عِنْدَنَا بَيْتٌ صَغِيرٌ.

exit.q: عِنْدَهُ means ...
Back to our ponder: 'with me is a brother': what does it show?
exit.a: Languages express the same idea differently.

lessons.homework: Write five عِنْدِي sentences about your family and home.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Common vocabulary: personal pronouns, my family, adjectives and moods
lessons.title: My and your: endings and the possessive construct
lessons.bigQuestion: How would you say 'the house of my grandfather' in two words?
objectives: To understand how to show possession with endings and with two nouns together (iḍāfah)
successCriteria: All: use ـِي، ـكَ، ـكِ، ـهُ، ـهَا on family nouns
Most: make iḍāfah phrases like بَيْتُ جَدِّي
Some: write sentences combining endings and iḍāfah
lessons.crossCurricular: English: possessive apostrophe compared with Arabic iḍāfah

keywords.def: possessive construct: two nouns together, 'X of Y'

hook.text: How would you say 'the house of my grandfather' in two words?
hook.a: بَيْتُ جَدِّي: the first noun loses ال, the second shows whose.

teach.heading: Endings
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Two nouns: iḍāfah
bullets: First noun: no ال, no tanwin

teach.heading: Spot the mistake
teach.note: Common error.

misconception.right: بَيْتُ جَدِّي: the first noun drops ال

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Iḍāfah: no ال and no tanwin on the first noun.

practice.model: Teacher: house = بَيْت, no ال: بَيْتُ. My aunt = خَالَتِي (ة → ت). Together: بَيْتُ خَالَتِي.

independent.q: Possession task on the pupil PDF: write eight phrases (four with endings, four with iḍāfah) about your family's things, then use three in full sentences (e.g. سَيَّارَةُ أَبِي بَيْضَاءُ).
independent.a: Correct phrases and agreement
independent.model: Teacher writes سَيَّارَةُ أَبِي and the sentence سَيَّارَةُ أَبِي بَيْضَاءُ.

independent.q: Extend: correct three wrong iḍāfah phrases.
independent.a: Drop ال and tanwin from the first noun

exit.q: In iḍāfah the first noun has ...
Back to our ponder: 'the house of my grandfather' in two words?

lessons.homework: Label five family items at home with iḍāfah phrases (e.g. كِتَابُ أُخْتِي).
lessons.send: SEND: noun + noun cards. EAL: pattern table. Stretch: three-word iḍāfah: بَيْتُ عَمِّ أَبِي.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Free time and my profile
lessons.title: Hobbies and free time
objectives: Name hobbies and say what you like and dislike
Use أُحِبُّ with a noun of action
Give a reason with لِأَنَّ
starter: Say 'This is my uncle's house' in Arabic.
Say 'I have a brother' in Arabic.
How do you ask 'whose is this?'

teach.heading: Hobby words
teach.note: Show pictures; pupils name them. Note: many hobbies are 'action nouns'. Mention that 'kurat al-qadam' is an idafa (ball of the foot). Pupils tick hobbies they enjoy.

teach.heading: I like
teach.note: Teach uhibbu + noun with fatha ending. Pupils produce sentences. Misconception: using أُحِبُّ without al- (e.g. أحب قراءة). Keep al- or an idafa.

teach.heading: Reasons
teach.note: Introduce reasons: useful (مُفِيدٌ), fun (مُمْتِعٌ), healthy (مُفِيدٌ لِلصِّحَّةِ). Notice li'annahaa/li'annahu depends on gender of the hobby. Provide sentence frames.

teach.heading: Where and when
teach.note: Add place and time details. Revise verbs أَلْعَبُ، أَقْرَأُ، أَسْبَحُ. Pupils build sentences with 'where' and 'when'.

teach.heading: Interview
teach.note: Teach هِوَايَةٌ (hobby) and the question. Pupils interview each other and record answers. Report back with 'his hobby/her hobby'.

practice: Ask a partner their name and age in Arabic.
Match hobbies with pictures and sentences.
Tell a partner two hobbies with reasons.
independent: Write 6 sentences about hobbies with reasons.
Survey three people and report their hobbies.
Create a poster: 'My free time' with Arabic labels.
exit: How do you say 'because it is useful'?
lessons.homework: Write a paragraph about your hobbies (6-8 sentences) with reasons.
lessons.send: SEND: hobby cards and sentence frames. EAL: bilingual word bank. Stretch: include frequency words (دَائِمًا، أَحْيَانًا) and compare hobbies with a partner.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Free time and my profile
lessons.title: My profile: writing and review
objectives: Write a connected paragraph about yourself and family
Use accurate agreement and connectives
Self-assess against success criteria
starter: Say 'I like swimming because it is useful' in Arabic.
Say 'her bag is big' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Review the unit
teach.note: Run through the unit quickly using a quiz. Ask pupils to pick the topic they feel least sure about. Use their answers to plan support.

teach.heading: Plan the paragraph
teach.note: Show a planning grid: pupils fill each box with 2-3 phrases. Model one completed paragraph. Highlight use of connectives: وَ، لَكِنْ، أَيْضًا.

teach.heading: Model text
teach.note: Read and annotate the model. Ask: what makes this good? (variety, accuracy, connectives). Ask pupils to highlight verbs and adjectives.

teach.heading: Success criteria
teach.note: Share the criteria. Pupils may use a word bank. Remind of common errors: gender, al-, the idafa. Set a timer for writing.

teach.heading: Peer review
teach.note: Pupils review a partner's paragraph and give a star and a wish. Teacher circulates and notes common errors for feedback next lesson.

practice: Write the Arabic for 'my brother is tall'.
Complete a planning grid for your paragraph.
independent: Write a paragraph about yourself and your family (10 sentences).
exit: Self-assess: which part is your best?
lessons.homework: Redraft your paragraph and record yourself reading it aloud.
lessons.send: SEND: paragraph frame with sentence starters. EAL: bilingual criteria. Stretch: write a second paragraph about your friend using third-person forms.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Common vocabulary: numbers, colours, clothes and shapes
lessons.title: Bridge: the Arabic letters and how they join
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do Arabic letters change shape?
objectives: To understand how Arabic letters change shape at the start, middle and end of a word
successCriteria: All: write ب in its start, middle and end forms
Most: name the six letters that never join to the next letter
Some: join letters into a word and split a word into letters
lessons.crossCurricular: English: handwriting joins; Arabic, like joined-up English, links letters in a word
lessons.smsc: Cultural: Arabic calligraphy as a great Muslim art

hook.text: Arabic is written right to left and most letters hold hands with the next one. Which letters do you think refuse to hold hands, and why might that be?
hook.a: Six letters: ا د ذ ر ز و never join to the letter after them.

islamicLink.text: The first revelation tells us that Allah 'taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know' (al-'Alaq 96:4-5). Writing Arabic well is a way to honour the language of the Qur'an.

starter.q: Bismillah. How many letters are in the Arabic alphabet? A) 26 B) 28 C) 30
Write any three Arabic letters you know.

teach.heading: Letters change shape
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Each letter has up to four forms. Most keep their 'head' and lose their 'tail' when joined.

teach.heading: Letters that do not join forward
bullets: ا د ذ ر ز و
They join to the letter before, never after
دَرْس (dars): د and ر stand apart from the next letter
teach.note: Teach a memory phrase: 'six stubborn letters'. Show وَرْدَة (wardah, rose): و and ر break the word into pieces.

teach.heading: Model: writing a word

model.problem: Write كَتَبَ (kataba, he wrote) from ك + ت + ب
steps: Join: كتب, then add the vowels: كَتَبَ

teach.note: Write live on the Teams whiteboard or under the visualiser.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Which letter never joins to the next letter?
check.why: ر is one of the six: ا د ذ ر ز و.

teach.heading: Dictation routine
bullets: Say the letters as you write
teach.note: From today every lesson has a short dictation (the school's Arabic intent). Words today: بَاب، دَرْس، قَلَم، وَرْدَة.

practice.q: Join the letters: ق + ل + م
practice.model:
ق at the start: قـ.
ل in the middle: ـلـ.
م at the end: ـم.
Joined: قلم.

practice.q: Why is there a gap in دار?
practice.a: د and ا do not join to the next letter.

independent.q: Core: Dictation: write the four words the teacher reads (بَاب، دَرْس، قَلَم، وَرْدَة), then copy each three times neatly.
independent.a: بَاب، دَرْس، قَلَم، وَرْدَة
independent.model: Teacher reads بَاب, says the letters ب ا ب and writes it, pointing out that ا does not join forward.

independent.q: Extend: Join: ك + ت + ا + ب and م + د + ر + س + ة.
independent.a: كتاب، مدرسة

independent.q: Stretch: Find three words in Surah al-Ikhlas that have a non-joining letter.
independent.a: For example: أَحَد، الصَّمَدُ، يُولَدْ

exit.q: How many forms can one Arabic letter have? A) 2 B) 4 C) 6
Big question: why do Arabic letters change shape?
exit.a: Because letters join; their form depends on whether they are at the start, middle or end of a word.

lessons.title: Bridge: short vowels, sukun, shaddah and tanwin
lessons.bigQuestion: How do the small marks above and below Arabic letters change how a word sounds?
objectives: To understand how short vowels and signs tell us exactly how to read an Arabic word
successCriteria: All: read a letter with fathah, dammah and kasrah
Most: read words with sukun and shaddah
Some: read and write the three kinds of tanwin
lessons.crossCurricular: English: phonics, where letters and sounds are matched
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the signs (harakat) were added so that everyone could read the Qur'an correctly

keywords.def: a short 'a' mark above the letter
a short 'u' mark above the letter
a short 'i' mark below the letter

hook.text: كتب can be read كَتَبَ (he wrote), كُتُب (books) or كُتِبَ (it was written). How could a reader know which one is meant?
hook.a: From the small vowel marks, or from the meaning of the sentence.

islamicLink.text: Allah sent the Qur'an in clear Arabic (ash-Shu'ara' 26:195). Early Muslim scholars added dots and vowel marks to the mushaf so that new Muslims would not misread it.

starter.q: Bismillah. Which letter does NOT join forward? A) د B) س C) ل

teach.heading: Three short vowels
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils say ba, bu, bi with the mouth shapes: open, round, smile.

teach.heading: Sukun and shaddah
teach.note: Pupils clap twice for a shaddah. Read: مُدَرِّس (mudarris, teacher).

teach.heading: Tanwin
teach.note: Tanwin marks a word as 'a' (indefinite). Note the extra alif with -an.

teach.heading: Model: reading a word
teach.note: Build the word sound by sound, then say it smoothly.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Fathah on ر gives ra; the shaddah on ب doubles it: rabb.

practice.model:
قَ = qa.
لَ = la.
مٌ = mun (tanwin dammah).
Together: qalamun.

practice.q: Which mark makes the letter double?

independent.q: Core: Dictation of six vowelled words (كَتَبَ، كُتُبٌ، مِنْ، رَبّ، مُدَرِّسٌ، بَابًا), then read them aloud to the teacher.
independent.a: كَتَبَ، كُتُبٌ، مِنْ، رَبّ، مُدَرِّسٌ، بَابًا
independent.model: Teacher reads كَتَبَ, writes ك ت ب, then adds three fathahs, saying ka-ta-ba.

independent.q: Extend: Add the vowels you hear: محمد (Muhammad), مسجد (masjid).
independent.a: مُحَمَّد، مَسْجِد

independent.q: Stretch: Write كِتَاب with each tanwin and say when each might be used.
independent.a: كِتَابٌ، كِتَابًا، كِتَابٍ: they show the word's job in the sentence (subject, object, after a preposition)

exit.q: Which mark means 'no vowel'? A) fathah B) sukun C) kasrah
Big question: how do the small marks change how a word sounds? Give one example.
exit.a: They give the vowels; e.g. كَتَبَ (kataba) and كُتُب (kutub) have the same letters but different vowels.

lessons.title: Bridge: days of the week and months of the year
lessons.bigQuestion: How do we say the date in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to name the days and months in Arabic and say today's day and month
successCriteria: All: say the seven days in order
Most: name the international months and three Hijri months
Some: say today's day and month in one sentence
lessons.crossCurricular: History: the Hijri calendar begins with the Prophet's ﷺ migration to Madinah
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: Allah set the months for worship, such as Ramadan and Hajj

hook.text: Today has two dates: one in January and one in an Islamic month. Why do Muslims need both calendars?
hook.a: The Hijri calendar for worship (Ramadan, Hajj); the international one for school and work.

islamicLink.text: Allah says the number of months with Him is twelve, four of them sacred (at-Tawbah 9:36). The Hijri calendar counts from the Hijrah to Madinah.

starter.q: Bismillah. Reply to صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ. A) صَبَاحُ النُّورِ B) مَسَاءُ النُّورِ

teach.heading: The days
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Sunday to Thursday come from the numbers one to five. Friday is the day of gathering (jumu'ah).

teach.heading: Months: January to June
teach.note: These names come from the English and French names, so they are easy to guess.

teach.heading: Months: July to December
teach.note: Some Arab countries use other names (for example كَانُون الثَّانِي for January); we learn the common ones.

teach.heading: Hijri months to know
bullets: رَمَضَان (Ramadan): the ninth, the month of fasting
ذُو الحِجَّةِ (Dhu l-Hijjah): the twelfth, the month of Hajj
teach.note: We are now in Sha'ban (شَعْبَان), the month before Ramadan.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: الخَمِيس comes from خَمْسَة, five: the fifth day.

practice.model:
Start with اليَوْمَ (today).
Add يَوْمُ (the day of).
Add the day: الاِثْنَيْنِ.

practice.q: Which Hijri month is the month of fasting?

independent.q: Core: Write the seven days and twelve international months in Arabic (use the slides).
independent.a: الأَحَد ... السَّبْت; يَنَايِر ... دِيسَمْبِر
independent.model: Teacher writes الأَحَد and يَنَايِر, sounding each letter, then the class continues.

independent.q: Extend: Write today's date in a sentence: اليَوْمَ يَوْمُ ... فِي شَهْرِ ...
independent.a: For example: اليَوْمَ يَوْمُ الاِثْنَيْنِ فِي شَهْرِ يَنَايِر.

independent.q: Stretch: Write your birthday month and the Hijri month we are in now.
independent.a: For example: شَهْرُ مِيلَادِي مَايُو. نَحْنُ فِي شَهْرِ شَعْبَان.

exit.q: What is يَنَايِر? A) January B) June C) July
Big question: say today's day and month in Arabic.
exit.a: For example: اليَوْمَ يَوْمُ الاِثْنَيْنِ فِي شَهْرِ يَنَايِر.

lessons.homework: Say the date in Arabic to someone at home each day this week; learn the months by heart.
lessons.send: SEND: day and month cards to put in order. EAL: calendar with English beside each Arabic name. Stretch: learn all twelve Hijri months in order.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Common vocabulary: numbers, colours, clothes and shapes
lessons.title: How many? Counting things with كَمْ
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I ask and answer 'how many?' in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to ask how many with كَمْ and answer with a number and a noun
successCriteria: All: ask كَمْ ...؟ with a noun
Most: answer with 3 to 10 and a plural noun, e.g. عِنْدِي ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ
Some: answer with 11 to 20 and a singular noun, e.g. خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ قَلَمًا
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: counting and recording data in a tally
lessons.smsc: Moral: being thankful for what we have and sharing it

hook.text: Count the books near you. Is it easy to say the number in Arabic? What else might change in the sentence?
hook.a: The noun changes too: after 3 to 10 it is plural; after 11 it is singular.

islamicLink.text: Allah says that if you tried to count His blessings you could never count them all (Ibrahim 14:34). Counting what we have reminds us to say alhamdulillah.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is ١٥? A) خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ B) خَمْسَة

teach.heading: Asking how many
bullets: How many books do you have?
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The noun after كَمْ is singular with tanwin fathah.

teach.heading: Answering: 3 to 10
teach.note: With 3 to 10 the noun is plural. These three nouns are masculine, so the number keeps its ة.

teach.heading: Answering: 11 to 20
bullets: عِنْدِي أَحَدَ عَشَرَ قَلَمًا: I have 11 pens
عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ كِتَابًا: I have 20 books
teach.note: Most pupils: use the patterns as models. Most able: feminine nouns flip the number form: ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Which is correct for 'I have four books'?
check.why: After 3 to 10 the noun is plural: كُتُبٍ.

teach.heading: A tally in Arabic
teach.note: Read the chart: كَمْ قَلَمًا؟ خَمْسَةُ أَقْلَامٍ. Pupils answer for books (ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ) and exercise books (أَرْبَعَةُ دَفَاتِرَ).

practice.model:
Start with عِنْدِي (I have).
6 is between 3 and 10: سِتَّةُ.
Then the plural noun: أَقْلَامٍ.

practice.q: Ask a girl how many books she has.

independent.q: Core: Count three kinds of things on your desk and write a question and answer for each (portal response box).
independent.a: For example: كَمْ قَلَمًا عِنْدَكَ؟ عِنْدِي أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْلَامٍ.
independent.model: Teacher counts books on their desk and writes: كَمْ كِتَابًا عِنْدَكَ؟ عِنْدِي ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ.

independent.q: Extend: Translate: I have 8 books. I have 12 pens.
independent.a: عِنْدِي ثَمَانِيَةُ كُتُبٍ. عِنْدِي اثْنَا عَشَرَ قَلَمًا.

independent.q: Stretch: Use a feminine noun: I have three cars (سَيَّارَة).
independent.a: عِنْدِي ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ (the number loses ة with a feminine noun)

exit.q: What does كَمْ mean? A) how many B) where C) who
Big question: ask and answer 'how many pens?' in Arabic.
exit.a: كَمْ قَلَمًا عِنْدَكَ؟ عِنْدِي خَمْسَةُ أَقْلَامٍ.

lessons.homework: Make a tally of five kinds of things in your room and write a كَمْ question and answer for each.
lessons.send: SEND: answer frame عِنْدِي ___ ___ with noun cards. EAL: picture cards for the nouns. Stretch: explain the 3 to 10 and 11 to 99 rules in English.

lessons.title: Colours: masculine and feminine forms
lessons.bigQuestion: Why does a colour word in Arabic have two forms?
objectives: To understand that Arabic colours have masculine and feminine forms and how they are made
successCriteria: All: name six colours in the masculine form
Most: give the feminine form, e.g. أَحْمَر → حَمْرَاء
Some: explain the pattern أَفْعَل → فَعْلَاء
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the variety of colours in creation is a sign of Allah

hook.text: In English 'red' never changes. In Arabic a red pen and a red car need different words. Why might a language do that?
hook.a: Arabic adjectives agree with the noun's gender; قَلَم is masculine, سَيَّارَة is feminine.

islamicLink.text: Allah says He brings out fruits of varying colours, and in the mountains are streaks of white and red of varying colours (Fatir 35:27). Colours are among His signs.

starter.q: Bismillah. كَمْ means: A) how many B) what

teach.heading: Colours
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Hold up coloured objects; pupils say the masculine form.

teach.heading: The pattern

steps: Find the root letters: ح م ر

teach.note: Every colour above follows the same pattern.

teach.heading: Colours ending in ـِيّ
teach.note: These come from nouns: بُنّ (coffee beans), بُرْتُقَال (orange fruit).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: أَفْعَل → فَعْلَاء: خ ض ر gives خَضْرَاء.

teach.heading: No tanwin on these colours

misconception.right: قَلَمٌ أَحْمَرُ: colours on the أَفْعَل and فَعْلَاء patterns never take tanwin

teach.note: Stretch point for most able; all pupils copy the correct form.

practice.model:
Root: ز ر ق.
Masculine أَفْعَل: أَزْرَق.
Feminine فَعْلَاء: زَرْقَاء.

independent.q: Core: Copy and complete the table of six colours, masculine and feminine.
independent.a: أَحْمَر حَمْرَاء؛ أَزْرَق زَرْقَاء؛ أَخْضَر خَضْرَاء؛ أَصْفَر صَفْرَاء؛ أَسْوَد سَوْدَاء؛ أَبْيَض بَيْضَاء
independent.model: Teacher completes أَسْوَد → سَوْدَاء, showing the root س و د.

independent.q: Extend: Dictation: write the colours the teacher reads: أَبْيَض، خَضْرَاء، أَزْرَق، صَفْرَاء.
independent.a: أَبْيَض، خَضْرَاء، أَزْرَق، صَفْرَاء

independent.q: Stretch: The colour of the dome of the Prophet's ﷺ Masjid is green. Which form (m or f) goes with قُبَّة (dome)? Write it.
independent.a: Feminine: قُبَّةٌ خَضْرَاءُ

exit.q: What is the feminine of أَبْيَض? A) بَيْضَاء B) أَبْيَضَة
Big question: why does a colour have two forms in Arabic?
exit.a: Because adjectives agree with the noun's gender: masculine أَفْعَل, feminine فَعْلَاء.

lessons.homework: Find six coloured things at home and write each colour in the masculine and feminine form.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Common vocabulary: numbers, colours, clothes and shapes
lessons.title: Describing things with colours
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I build a sentence that describes the colour of something?
objectives: To understand how to place a colour after a noun so that it agrees in gender
successCriteria: All: say هٰذَا قَلَمٌ أَحْمَرُ
Most: choose the right form for masculine and feminine nouns
Some: describe with the definite: القَلَمُ أَحْمَرُ (the pen is red)
lessons.crossCurricular: English: adjective order (English puts colour before the noun; Arabic after)
lessons.smsc: Social: describing things clearly helps others

hook.text: English says 'a red car'. Arabic says 'a car red'. Which order seems more logical to you, and why?
hook.a: Arabic names the thing first, then describes it.

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us that the variety of colours on the earth is a lesson for those who reflect (an-Nahl 16:13). Describing colours accurately trains us to notice His signs.

starter.q: Bismillah. Feminine of أَحْمَر? A) حَمْرَاء B) أَحْمَرَة

teach.heading: Noun first, colour second
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The colour copies the noun's gender.

teach.heading: Model: a feminine noun
teach.note: Talk through each choice.

teach.heading: The thing is red
bullets: القَلَمُ أَحْمَرُ (al-qalamu ahmaru): the pen is red
السَّيَّارَةُ بَيْضَاءُ: the car is white
al- on the noun, no al- on the colour: a full sentence
teach.note: Compare: قَلَمٌ أَحْمَرُ (a red pen) and القَلَمُ أَحْمَرُ (the pen is red).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Which is correct for 'this is a green book'?
check.why: كِتَاب is masculine: هٰذَا and أَخْضَرُ, colour after the noun.

teach.heading: Sort: which colour form?
teach.note: Pupils show 1 or 2 fingers for each noun.

practice.q: Say: This is a white door (بَاب).
practice.model:
بَاب has no ة: masculine, so هٰذَا.
White masculine: أَبْيَض.
Colour after the noun: هٰذَا بَابٌ أَبْيَضُ.

practice.q: Say: This is a yellow flower (وَرْدَة).

independent.q: Core: Write five sentences describing things in your room with هٰذَا or هٰذِهِ and a colour.
independent.a: For example: هٰذَا كِتَابٌ أَزْرَقُ. هٰذِهِ حَقِيبَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ. هٰذَا بَابٌ أَبْيَضُ. هٰذِهِ طَاوِلَةٌ بُنِّيَّةٌ. هٰذَا قَلَمٌ أَحْمَرُ.
independent.model: Teacher holds up a black bag: feminine, so هٰذِهِ حَقِيبَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ.

independent.q: Extend: Turn two of your sentences into 'the ... is ...' sentences.
independent.a: For example: الكِتَابُ أَزْرَقُ. الحَقِيبَةُ سَوْدَاءُ.

independent.q: Stretch: Describe the flag of a Muslim country in Arabic (colours only).
independent.a: For example: عَلَمُ تُرْكِيَا أَحْمَرُ وَأَبْيَضُ.

exit.q: Where does the colour go in Arabic? A) before the noun B) after the noun
Big question: describe something near you with its colour in Arabic.

hook.text: Allah calls one kind of clothing 'the best clothing'. What do you think it is?
hook.a: The clothing of taqwa, righteousness (al-A'raf 7:26).

islamicLink.text: Allah says He has sent down clothing to cover us and as adornment, 'but the clothing of righteousness: that is best' (al-A'raf 7:26).

starter.q: Bismillah. 'A red car' is: A) سَيَّارَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ B) سَيَّارَةٌ أَحْمَرُ

teach.heading: Clothes
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils show one item on camera and name it.

teach.heading: I wear
bullets: أَلْبَسُ قَمِيصًا (albasu qamisan): I wear a shirt
After أَلْبَسُ: the item ends in -an
teach.note: The item is the object of the verb, so it takes tanwin fathah.

teach.heading: Model: adding a colour

model.problem: I wear a white thobe on Friday.
steps: أَبْيَضَ (white, masculine, object form, no tanwin)

teach.note: Colours on the أَفْعَل pattern take fathah without tanwin.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: أَلْبَسُ = I wear; مِعْطَفًا = a coat.

teach.heading: My clothes are ...
bullets: قَمِيصِي أَزْرَقُ: my shirt is blue
حِذَائِي أَسْوَدُ: my shoes are black
قُبَّعَتِي حَمْرَاءُ: my cap is red (feminine)
teach.note: Possessive -i (my) from Years 3 to 6; the colour agrees.

practice.q: Say: I wear a black coat.
practice.model:
أَلْبَسُ.
مِعْطَفًا (object).

hook.text: English has one word for 'you'. Arabic has different words for a boy and a girl. Why might that be useful?
hook.a: It is clearer who you are speaking to: أَنْتَ for a boy, أَنْتِ for a girl.

teach.note: Girl pronoun → girl adjective.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: To a girl: أَنْتِ with a feminine adjective.

practice.q: Say: he is a student; she is a student.

independent.q: Pronoun sentences on the pupil PDF: complete eight sentences with the right pronoun and adjective form, then write three about people you know (no names needed: هُوَ / هِيَ).

independent.q: Extend: say three sentences about yourself with أَنَا.

independent.q: Stretch: why does أَنَا stay the same for boys and girls?
independent.a: 'I' is the same; only the adjective changes: أَنَا طَالِبٌ / أَنَا طَالِبَةٌ.

exit.q: 'She' is ...
Back to our ponder: why two words for 'you'?
exit.a: It shows clearly whether you speak to a boy or a girl.

hook.text: English has one word 'uncle'. Arabic has two. Which is more useful, and why?
hook.a: Arabic tells you which side of the family: عَمّ (father's side), خَال (mother's side).

hook.text: What should a Muslim say first when asked 'How are you?', even on a hard day?
hook.a: الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ: praise Allah in every state, then say how you feel honestly.

islamicLink.text: When asked how they are, Muslims often begin with الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ, thanking Allah in every state.

teach.heading: How are you?
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Feelings
bullets: بِخَيْرٍ وَالحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ: fine, praise be to Allah

- أَنَا مُتْعَبَةٌ قَلِيلًا، وَالحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ.

hook.text: In Arabic every object is 'he' or 'she'. How would you know which to use for a book or a bag?
hook.a: Words ending in ة are usually feminine (هِيَ): حَقِيبَة; others are usually masculine (هُوَ): كِتَاب.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And He is with you wherever you are' (al-Hadid 57:4).

starter.q: 'The garden is behind the house' is ...

starter.a: فِي، عَلَى، تَحْتَ، فَوْقَ، أَمَامَ، خَلْفَ، بِجَانِبِ، بَيْنَ

teach.heading: Asking where
bullets: أَيْنَ الكِتَابُ؟ Where is the book?
هُوَ عَلَى المَكْتَبِ: it is on the desk
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: هُوَ or هِيَ?
teach.note: Pupils show the column number.

teach.heading: A dialogue

quote.text:
أَيْنَ مِفْتَاحِي؟

إِذَنْ هُوَ فِي حَقِيبَتِكَ.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: أَيْنَ السَّاعَةُ؟ The best answer is ...

practice.q: Answer: أَيْنَ القَلَمُ؟ (it is in the bag)

independent.model: Teacher models with a pupil: أَيْنَ النَّظَّارَةُ؟ هِيَ عَلَى الكِتَابِ.

independent.q: Extend: add لَيْسَ هُنَا (it is not here) to one exchange.
independent.a: For example: لَا، لَيْسَ هُنَا. هُوَ هُنَاكَ.

exit.q: أَيْنَ means ...

exit.a: Words with ة are usually هِيَ; others usually هُوَ

hook.text: Arabic has two words for 'what?'. Why might a language need two?
hook.a: One goes before nouns (مَا هٰذَا؟) and one before verbs (مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ؟).

teach.heading: مَا or مَاذَا?
teach.note: Pupils show 1 or 2.

teach.heading: Answer in full
teach.note: Model turning the question into an answer.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: تَشْرَبُ is a verb, so مَاذَا.

practice.q: Answer in full: مَاذَا تَكْتُبُ؟ (I am writing a letter)
